intended_object: The comodule morphism P → M ⊗_R C that corresponds to an R-linear map g : P → M under the cofree comodule adjunction. It is (g ⊗ id_C) ∘ ρ_P, viewed here in the category of finitely generated comodules. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the `cofreeLift_apply` lemma.
explanation:
The body wraps `Comodule.Hom.cofreeLift g` as a morphism of finitely generated comodules. `Comodule.Hom.cofreeLift g` is defined as `cofreeMap g ∘ cofreeUnit P`, which is (g ⊗ id) ∘ ρ_P (`cofreeLift_toLinearMap`, proved by `rfl`). This is the standard adjunct of g under the cofree comodule universal property (Sweedler, Chapter 2). The file also shows it is the inverse of the cofree hom-equivalence (`cofreeEquiv`).

The construction itself is stated over any commutative semiring and any coalgebra. Restricting to `FGComoduleCat`, with the hypothesis `Module.Finite R (M ⊗[R] C)`, is the whole point of this declaration: it is the finite-category version of the general lift, which the library also defines in full generality. So it is not too narrow.

As far as I can tell, Mathlib has no comodule category or cofree-comodule lift, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
